question: At m = 4 and surplus 0, does the closure refutation degree stay at 4 for l = 4, 5, 6 on the chained S3 system, and is the refutation degree of the FGHR-symmetrised S5 system (4l - 3 unknowns) flat in l or rising by about one per step?
decision_value: Every m = 4, l >= 4 degree measured so far is at surplus -3 to -9, while ECC2K-130's route sits at surplus about 0, and no FGHR-symmetrised m = 4 system has ever been run. If the chained system holds degree 4 at surplus 0 through l = 5 (or 6), the ECC2K-130 degree-4 row (2^68.43, +7.62 bits over rho, unconverted) regains support there and the next spend is K and the symmetry constants; if it rises, that row is withdrawn at surplus 0 and the degree-5 row (+10.32 bits) loses its last support. On the FGHR arm, a flat degree of at most 6 adds a row whose oracle term at l = 33 (2^28.1-2^32.5) is below the chained degree-5 term (2^36.2), a flat degree of 8 or more or a degree that rises with l closes FGHR as a rescue for m = 4. The equivariant C3 blocks decide only how far l the FGHR arm can be pushed on a given host. A result that leaves all of these unchanged (e.g. FGHR input degree 8 or 9 and arm A at degree 4) still ends this card: it is then recorded as a mechanism result and no larger host is bought.

resources.notes: Host (a), this host: 32 vCPU Xeon 6975P with AVX-512, 124 GB, 2 TB EBS, shared with a multi-day job, so at most 4 concurrent single-threaded jobs and 100 GB in total. It runs stages S0-S2: arm A closure at (16,4) and (20,5) (10 and 61 GB derived from the measured 0.222 x cols^2 bytes), msolve on (13,4), (13,5) (2.8-12.6 GB band) and a 6 h sizing probe at (16,4), arm B at l = 4, 5, 6 (under 4 GB plain to l = 5; 54 GB at l = 6, degree 10 with C3 blocks). The 350 core-hours are dominated by msolve's upper band under a 72 h wall per draw; the closure and arm B together are under 60. Host (b): a 512 GB host (32-64 vCPU, 500 GB disk) for stage S3 only: arm A at (24,6), N = 72, about 264 GB (after M3) or msolve multi-threaded; arm B at (28,7) to degree 8 and (32,8) to degree 7 with C3 blocks (161-235 GB); about 100-200 core-hours plus what the msolve probe justifies. A 1 TB host is needed only if the FGHR input degree is 9 and (28,7) is wanted at degree 9 (about 0.73 TB with blocks); not proposed. Arm A at degree 5 fits no host considered (0.8 TB at (16,4)). Derivation: README.md section 5.

params.argv_note: --to 0 and --max-cols 0 mean unbounded for the msolve engine (msolve has no degree bound; its caps are prlimit and the wall). Shard 1 replays the committed 06 exports (seed 20261014, unsat indices 0-3); shard 2 is the sizing probe of PROTOCOL section 4 (6 h wall, not a reading). Shards 5 and 6 run on host (b) only, after gate G3; shard 5 needs M3 (N = 72 > 64). The msolve runs at (15,6) and (20,5) are added as shards only if the shard-2 probe projects they fit; that amendment is made before the freeze.

outputs.result_schema: m4_formulations JSONL, one line per (arm, draw): arm, cell, draw, basis, x_r, n_vars, d_sys, exact solution count, and per degree xl_refuted, closure_refuted, saturated, xl_rank, closure_rank, columns, closure_products, closure_word_ops, secs; msolve lines add per-round degree and matrix size, max_degree, gb_is_one, peak_rss_kb; c3 lines add the E1-E5 identity fields

cairn.notes: Seven single heavy runs, one lab task per shard. The harness writes one line per (arm, draw) and --resume skips finished ones, so a shard is preemptible between draws (a draw in progress is lost). Shards 0-4 on host (a); shards 5-6 need host (b) and gate G3 (owner approval).

env.recipe: A rust image with the pinned commit checked out and `cargo build --release --example m4_formulations --example msolve_degree_log --example dreg_ladder --example dreg_closure --example ic_next10_06_chain_export` baked in, plus msolve v0.6.5 built from source (research/dreg_closure_m4l6_20261018/pod/boot.sh:85-89), then `cairn lab env import crypto-m4-degree --docker <image>`

exec.sandbox_reason: working sets of 10-100 GB on host (a) and up to about 300 GB on host (b); the jails' memory limits are untested at that size and a host-level kill would read as an infrastructure error; the receipt records the run as unconfined

funding.rationale: Exponent-level for the binary (ECC2K-130) route, below PKM lead 1 (1,000,000) because part of the question is already read (closure 4 at l <= 6, surplus <= -3) and stages S0-S2 run on a host already owned; above the Kummer P-224 depth card (400,000) because it can add or withdraw an ECC2K-130 price row.

owner_hint: S0-S2 on the 124 GB host by whoever builds M0-M2; S3 by whoever has a 512 GB host
